Do you see that? It's just before the word "opinion" in your language. Can you find the word "opinion"? Look at the paragraph above that. It says: "Bearing in mind the validity of the facts and data presented, which are based exclusively on the available written documentation and the intelligence acquired through oral statements, eye-witness accounts of the participants in the event where there is no submission of written statements, complaints or other type of substantiating statements to the Ministry of the Interior about the actual event," and then it says: "The commission gives the following opinion." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm with you. But the -- there's something left out. It's the verbal expressions not written. That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you reading from the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm reading in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is there something I've read in English that you feel is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I wasn't following you in English, since I don't understand it well, but quoting from the written, you have said that in the informations acquired in writing while it reads here "information verbally acquired."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're right, you're absolutely right, because it then says where there -- it says, "The intelligence acquired through oral statements, eye-witness accounts of the participants in the event where there is no submission of written statements, complaints or other type of substantiating statements to the Ministry of the Interior about the actual event," and then we see the word "opinion." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The opinion reads like this: "The activities which were carried out by the Security Forces of the Ministry of the Interior to repulse the armed attacks of the terrorist groups on 12 August 2001 in the village of Ljuboten-Skopje were well-founded, justified and properly undertaken, yet there is evidently a slight tolerable degree of individual overstepping of the boundaries of the prescribed powers carried out by a small number of members of the Ministry of the Interior who actively participated in the event." Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the next paragraph, which is at the top of page 6, General, in your version, "Given the absence of written documentation from the investigation, an autopsy of the bodies found in the village of Ljuboten-Skopje, and in order to achieve comprehensiveness and all-exclusiveness it is necessary for the authorities in the Republic of Macedonia to undertake legal action, the exhumation of the bodies in the presence of experts and of representatives of interested international organisations which will have as a result the taking of all necessary legal actions towards confirmation, all the relevant facts and receipt of an answer to the open substantive question about this event." General, this is -- is this the report that the commission produced at the end of its work?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did we clarify its date, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the best of the Prosecution's knowledge, it is it dated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. The witness, does he know, can he help?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, the witness said to the best of what he could see, it appeared to be 4 September 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. It will be received. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to ask to maybe verify the translation of the last paragraph, the one preceding the opinion, because although I do not understand -- I don't speak Macedonian, in the English translation I saw that in this translation it is mentioned twice the word "written statements," while the Macedonian version in the last sentence, it reads about written submissions, which are not statements at all. My objection goes in line that the English translation should be made in line with the Macedonian version that I just read out, because instead of statement, the word "written complaint" should be put. That changes the sense of the text that was just read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the word "complaint" exists in that paragraph in English. There is a phrase said, "Where there is no submission of written statements, complaints or other type of substantiating statements to the Ministry of the Interior."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I see that, but the Macedonian version never mentions the word "statement," while the lower part in the English, the word "statement" is mentioned twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, this is a final translation from CLSS, but we can certainly ask them to review this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be received as Exhibit P378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, you mentioned earlier in your testimony regarding the work of the commission that there wasn't much that the commission could do. What investigative work did the commission do?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I think that I have already replied to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a couple of specific questions then. Do you recall whether the commission spoke to any of the ethnic Albanians who were detained in and around Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001. Let me rephrase my question. Did the commission attempt to speak with any of the detained ethnic Albanian residents of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I personally didn't, but the offices working in the field who spoke with them made all the written materials available to the commission, actually the president of the commission, Mr. Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see the officers in the field who spoke to them. Who is them? Who was spoken to?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I think that the question was who spoke with the detainees in the police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: In the police station, if you wish, I could give you a more elaborate answer, who are the persons who question the persons who are detained in the police station. According to the applicable legislation in the Republic of Macedonia, when the legal requirements are met, the authorised officers have the right and duty to detain a person and when a person is brought in, in a station, then the duty officer admits that person and conducts the initial interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would sometimes a criminal inspector conduct an initial interview?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Can I continue where I stopped in order to explain the situation to you more vividly?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: So the duty officer admits the person regardless who has brought the person in. These persons could be ordinary citizens, actually, if a citizen is found in in flagrante situation in perpetration of a criminal act, the duty officer conducts the initial interview in order to assess who should then take the person over. If it is a situation of less severe violation of laws, as we call it misdemeanour, traffic misdemeanour, public order misdemeanour or any misdemeanour, the case is then processed by the uniformed police, while if a law -- if an article of the criminal code is violated then is the criminal police that handles the case, which mean that the duty officer is obligated to call a colleague from the hierarchy who covers that topical area, the topical area covering the issue that the person had infringed and the person could later be a suspect or an indicted person, which means that for a case in question now, the authorised officers, actually the only authorised officers, are those from the criminal police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so would an inspector from the criminal police then interview someone who has been detained for a serious crime?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. Not only they could, they have the duty to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would that be standard procedure for that inspector to send an Official Note or a report up the chain of command regarding the interview?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they have a duty to submit an Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are such Official Notes the kind of materials that your committee reviewed prior to producing their report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Let me repeat. I did not view them personally because this is not within my job description. But certainly, Mr. Petrovski and of course the president of the committee had seen them. I've learned this from the discussions that I had with Mr. Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to ask you, General, to turn to what is tab 3 in your binder. This is 65 ter number 285.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, don't worry, Your Honours, I'm not going to review every item in this 65 ter number, just a limited selection, I promise. Mr. Usher, I think we may need your help, if you could stay with the witness, because this is some fairly lengthy material that is divided up into separate documents. If we turn to -- this is material that was received by the Office of the Prosecutor pursuant to a request for assistance to the government of Macedonia asking for information pertaining to a second committee that was formed to investigate the events in Ljuboten village in August of 2001. And perhaps if Mr. Galevski could be shown what is pages 8 to 9. It's 65 ter number 285.5. It starts with ERN number N000-8907. And if General Galevski could be shown the Macedonian version, please, so he can follow along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, this is a decision dated the 7th of March, 2003, commission of -- "On establishment of a commission, a commission of inquiry into the circumstances and facts related to the events and incidents which took place in the territory of Ljuboten village, Skopje, August 2001 was hereby established within the Ministry of Interior, consisting of the following members." Are you with me? Do you see what I've read?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first name is it Major-General Zoran Jovanovski, under-secretary in the police department, chairman, and then there are several other names below General Jovanovski's name. And if you turn the page to the next page, the next page in the English version, part two says, "The commission shall have the task to investigate and analyse all materials and documents related to the events which took place in the territory of Ljuboten-Skopje in August 2001, ascertain the composition and capacity of the unit which took action in this period, including the identity of each of its members individually, establish the causes and circumstances surrounding the deaths of the victims and the material damage inflicted, in order to establish the truth about the aforementioned events," et cetera. And then in section 3: "The commission shall prepare a report on its activities and submit it to the minister of the interior no later than 2 May 2003." And then we see down below that at this time in spring of 2002 the minister of the interior was Hari Kostov. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page which is 65 ter 285.6?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this way of asking questions. We do not see at all what is the basis for the Prosecutor to ask these questions, because as far as we can see this is a document that is it outside of the scope of the indictment 7th of March, 2003. We do not know whether this witness knows -- actually, maybe this would be a way that the learned colleague could frame his question about the existence of another committee or anything, because we do not see here any foundation for the aforementioned document to be shown to this witness. Furthermore, the first person mentioned here General Major Zoran Jovanovski is a person who is in the list of Prosecutor's witness and he could be shown all these documents, and for these reasons we object before establishing the foundation for this witness to be able to say anything about these documents, we object to questions being asked of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I start --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can start with the second objection first. Yes, General Zoran Jovanovski will be called as a witness and yes, he will be shown these documents. I'm only going to seek to mark these documents for identification at this time. Your Honours, as you know, one of the important issues of this case is whether the accused took reasonable and adequate measures to investigate the alleged crimes in Ljuboten, and punish the perpetrators. Therefore, the work of the committee that Mr. Boskoski set up is obviously of crucial interest, I believe, to the Trial Chamber, and what I want to pursue with this witness is whether the -- some of the work done by this second committee was also done by the first committee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We see no reason, Ms. Residovic, to interfere with the line of questioning at the moment. But we do see the time, and we must now take the second break. So we will resume at five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And according to the Prosecution's calculations, I have one hour and 20 minutes to complete my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As you know, that cannot all be done this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour, yes. I had asked to see 65 ter 285.6. On the screen we see what is apparently the Macedonian version twice, and I'm wondering whether there is an English version. But I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No English, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, the parties have the English version in their binders, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At tab?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is part of tab 3. This is part of tab 3, and it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, this is a document from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, from the investigation committee about the events and happenings in the village Ljuboten. It's dated 25 November 2003. It's part of the work of this second investigation committee established by Minister Kosta. We see it is entitled information on the activities undertaken by the investigation committee about the events and happenings in the village of Ljuboten. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please take a look at the second paragraph that begins: "At the first meeting." Paragraph reads: "At the first meeting that was held on 12 November 2003 attended by all members of the committee a conversation was carried out with Johan Tarculovski and the owner of the security agency Kometa, Zoran Jovanovski, alias Bucuk. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We barely hear the witness so if you could speak --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Need to give an oral answer, General, you need to speak up.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the members of your committee interview Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the members of your committee interview the owner of the Kometa security agency, Zoran Jovanovski, also known as Bucuk?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn to what is 65 ter 285.11. It's the 25th page in the English version. And if the usher could assist the witness to see the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this is an Official Note. It says at the top "submitted by Staff-Sergeant Miodrag Stojanovski, policeman, administer." Do you see that at the top?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is dated 20 November 2003. Subject, weapons issued to volunteers in 2001. And it says this: "On 25 July 2001, a group from the Kometa agency led by Johan Tarculovski employed at the security sector of the RM MVR arrived at the police station OOV. They presented a list to Commander Georgi Dimitrov and asked to be issued with weapons as volunteer police reservists. The commander, having consulted his superiors at the security sector, ordered me to issue the weapons. Half of the men from the list were issued with weapons on 25 July 2001 and the other half on 26 July 2001, after which they were sent to the security training centre to join other volunteers and fill out the questionnaires for police reservists." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In August/September 2001, did your committee interview Miodrag Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about any of this or that I see any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you turn the page, and this would be now 65 ter 285.12, it's an Official Note, a bit longer this time. No, that's not it. Hmm. Perhaps we could look at 285.13, and if I could ask the usher's assistance, please. No. I'm having a technical problem. I'm going to move on. I'm going to skip this, please. If we could simply move on to what should be 285.24. This is a report dated the 6th of May, 2003, from the Ministry of Interior, sector for analysis and research. And again it's a report on the meeting of the commission investigating the events in Ljuboten village, and it's a couple of pages long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, just to make sure that I understand you and your testimony is clear, is it your testimony that the information that your committee received, it was information received in writing from various sources of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the official writs that the MOI received, but not such official notes. That were written much later than the time when we were operating as a committee. But while -- why were they written then, this is a question in itself, because some of these Official Notes, if these events actually happened, the police officers had the duty to write them then, immediately and not three or four years later than the actual events taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could your committee have spoken with these police officers, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I didn't directly but my subordinates in charge of the uniformed police in the city did, especially with the police officers in the region Cair, certainly, and I must mention the names that were read in the previous information in the previous document, I have heard mentioned for the first time when I was interviewed by the ICTY investigator. I'm not sure whether it was the first or the second interview. At that time, then nobody mentioned any such names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to mark 65 ter 285 for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P379, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn now to what is tab 4 in the binder in front of you, General Galevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is, Your Honours, from 65 ter 257, which I will again simply to be marked for identification. If General Galevski could be shown the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a report to the government of "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia" on a visit to "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia" carried out by the European committee for the prevention of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, also known as the CPT from 21 to 26 October 2001. And if you turn to the third page, General, you will find the table of contents. And I'd like to direct your attention, please, to subsection D where it says cooperation between the CPT and the authorities of "the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could the General's right microphone be turned on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see that in subchapter D there are sections on consultations at the central level and then a second section called cooperation at the local level. A is places of detention, B is judicial authorities at the Basic Court in Skopje, C is the institute of forensic medicine and medical professionals at hospitals in Skopje. Do you see that, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then in part two we see it's called facts found during the visit and action proposed. Underneath that we see a subheading, A, torture and other forms of ill-treatment and then we see subsection 4, it's called the Ljuboten cases. Do you see that, General.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you could turn to what is page 8 in the English version; it's page 7 in the Macedonian version. Are you on page 7, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm on page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see at the top of the page a letter B, establishments visited and then below that number 3, the delegation visited the following places of detention. And then there's a heading police stations and we see a number of police stations in the list, including Bit Pazar police station, Skopje; Cair police station, Skopje; Gazi Baba police station, Skopje; Karpos police station, Skopje; Kisela Voda police station, Skopje. Do you see that, general?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then if you could look at the bottom of page eight in the Macedonian version, this is the middle of page nine in the English version, there is a section entitled cooperation between the CPT and the authorities of the "the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia." Then we see, one, consultations at central level. Do you see where I'm reading, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 says: "In the course of its visit, the delegation Ilinka Mitreva, the minister for foreign affairs, as well as senior officials from the ministries of justice, interior, and foreign affairs. In particular, fruitful discussions on police matters were held with the following officials from the minister of the interior, Goran Mitevski, director of the bureau for public security; General Risto Galevski, head of the police station," et cetera. Do you recall meeting with this delegation in October of 2001, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I don't deny it, but I do not remember because I will repeat again, the events taking place, the people I have meet were really numerous, so I could not remember them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right, that's fine. If we could turn to what is page 19 in the English version. This is the bottom of page 17 in the Macedonian version, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I'm looking for page 19 in the English version; we have 21 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you see there's a number four and then it says: "The Ljuboten cases." Do you see that? This would be the bottom of page 17 in your language.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 27 begins: "The CPT's delegation examined a series of cases of alleged ill-treatment emerging in the aftermath of an operation by government Security Forces in the village of Ljuboten near Skopje on 10 to 12 August 2001. The delegation focussed its attention on the treatment of those persons who had been deprived of their liberty by the police in the course of or after the Ljuboten operation." Are you following with me, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, can I follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Further down in that paragraph there's a sentence beginning with: "In addition." And so the rest of the paragraph reads like this: "In addition to the other information gathering activities it undertook to this end, e.g., visits to Cair, Karpos and Kisela Voda police stations, and examination of prison and medical records, the delegation held lengthy discussions with senior officials of the Ministry of the Interior, including the director of the bureau of public security, the head of the police division, the head of the internal control department." So, again, that's another reference to you, would that be fair, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: No, I can't confirm because I don't see it here what are you reading from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you reading paragraph 27?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can the usher please assist the General.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Cases -- the Ljuboten cases. I was able to follow the first part and then when you turned the page I lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn -- I'm sorry. Can you turn to the end of paragraph 27. Do you see the phrase "the head of the police division." Do you see that there? It's in the second-to-the-last sentence, the penultimate sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment, the answer was barely audible, we are not aware what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, do you see phrase "the delegation held lengthy discussions with senior officials of the Ministry of Interior." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see halfway down that paragraph: "In addition to the other information gathering activities."

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to be the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you on page 17?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. 17 ends with a lengthy sentence where the item 4 says the Ljuboten cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next paragraph, does that begin with the words "the CPT's delegation"?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: No paragraph starts with "delegation."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does paragraph 27 begin with?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: "KZT delegation, this is the Macedonian abbreviation, interpreter's comment, that this is at the very beginning after the number 27."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you then see the second sentence begins "the delegation focussed its attention." Do you see that, second sentence?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is it correct. This is on page 17, not 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So see if you can follow with me now. "It has been alleged that villagers had fled their homes during and immediately after the security operation." Can you follow with me there?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then there's a sentence: "The men, some 100 of them, were allegedly beaten close to the check-point and then taken to the three police stations in the capital." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "... Where the beatings increased in severity." And then it says, "In addition to the other information gathering activities it undertook, that is, visits to Cair, Karpos and Kisela Voda police stations, an examination of prison and medical records," are you following with me now?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "The delegation held length discussions with senior officials of the Ministry of the Interior." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And one of the senior officials mentioned is the head of the police division. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At that time that would have been you, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you -- could you now focus on paragraph 29 and this is on page 20 of the English version. It's page 19 in the Macedonian version. Paragraph 29 refers to the commission set up on the 13th of August, 2001 by the minister of the interior in order to examine the circumstances and analyse the activities undertaken by the Security Forces the Ministry of the Interior to repel the armed attacks by terrorist groups on 12 August 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then below that it appears to quote the report of your committee. It says: "The ad hoc committee expressed its opinion in a document dated 4 September 2001 addressed to the minister for the interior that, quote, the activities undertaken by the Ministry for the Interior are well-founded, justified and legitimately implemented, though it has been noted that there was a negligible or tolerable degree of individual deviation from the limits of authorised action on the part of a small number of members of the Ministry of Interior who actively participated in the operation in question." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, if you move down to Paragraph 30 we see the following. This is still on page 20 of the English version at the bottom of the page. "Notwithstanding the assessment by the ad hoc committee of the Ministry of Interior, medical evidence collected by the delegation was consistent with allegations of ill-treatment of the persons deprived of their liberty in the context of or following the operation of government Security Forces in Ljuboten." Do you see paragraph 30, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment, it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you say yes?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. You need to speak up for the interpreters. In the middle of page 19 in your version, General, top of page 21 in the English version, we see case five,, And according to case five, the first paragraph, it says: "A remand prisoner claimed that at the time of his apprehension in Ljuboten on 12 August 2001 he was kicked on various parts of the body by special police officers. He alleged that officers continued to kick him and strike him with the butts of their fire-arms on the way to the police station in Mirkovci and that the ill-treatment continued at that establishment." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He also stated that at one point special police carved the shape of a cross into his back with a bayonet?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we ask the Prosecutor to tell us at least what is the question for the witness, considering that we are now reading about the cases and it is not the problem for us to hear what is written there read, but my concern is what is the question of the Prosecutor in relation to what he's reading now to the witness, especially since the report is compiled a year later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although the events took place earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The question, Your Honour, which will come in about two minutes will be whether the committee that this witness participated on also consulted the medical records at Skopje city hospital that are mentioned two paragraphs below the lines that I just read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next paragraph refers to the hospital record from Skopje city hospital of this person. And then it says in the following paragraph: "An unusual feature." Do you see that, General Galevski, there is a phrase beginning with the paragraph "an unusual feature." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says this: "An unusual feature of the person's report at city hospital was that under the heading reasons given by the patient for seeking medical attention, the typed phrase "he was beaten by the police," could be discerned underneath the row of Xs which had been typed over it. In the space above the Xs the words 'for pain in the chest and in the abdomen' had been typed. The delegation found that certain other medical records at this hospital contained similar alterations (by overtyping with Xs) of an initial entry reading 'he was beaten by the police.'" Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell me, General, did your committee consult the medical records of the persons who were detained at Ljuboten and then later treated at Skopje city hospital?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Personally I have not participated in such a checkups because if such checkups are made, these are made by specially trained persons for violation of -- violations of this type who are authorised to contact the medical personnel. It is it impossible for everyone to go in a hospital and investigate, especially if wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Tell us, General, suppose you had seen these records that the delegation from the committee for the prevention of torture had seen, these altered records from Skopje city hospital, do you think that would have been relevant to the opinions in the report produced by your commission?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I don't -- I do not know when this report was received by the Ministry of Interior. It is not -- surely not at the time when the report was written. It must have been quite later, in order to have it as a relevant source of information, and surely if we would have received it in time, we would have surely taken some actions in -- within our departments and our services.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General, perhaps my question wasn't clear. You see, persons who were detained at Ljuboten were subsequently treated at Skopje city hospital beginning on the 13th of August. So my question was, if your committee had seen the records that were produced related to these injured persons from the 13th, 14th, 15th of August at Skopje city hospital, would that have been relevant to the opinion expressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Surely, but those people must have reported first within -- in the Ministry of Interior because they were publicly called if they had any comments to come and report, but no such report was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Suppose they're dead. If you're dead, it's difficult to make a report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Am I suppose to comment this remark of yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: If I die, my sons would surely report or the wife or some of the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Because Ljuboten is a lively village, densely populated, then surely someone have seen something or have reported something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if someone dies, either in police custody or after being taken to Skopje city hospital by the police, would -- the police would have written reports about that death, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: The police wouldn't have written it if the person had died in a hospital, but that would have been written by the medical personnel, especially in the forensics department whereby the causes of death would have been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's talk about that. Can you turn to page 21 of the Macedonian version, please, page 22 of the English version. The top of page 21, General Galevski, there is a subheading it says case 8, AQ. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I'm at page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 21, at the top of the page case 8 --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, 21. What I can see at the bottom is case 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you turn the page. Turn the page, please. On the next page, do you see case 8?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: No, I cannot see case 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Before you walk away, can we please just find number 8?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] Case 8, AQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first paragraph of AQ, case 8 says: "Reference should also be made to the case of Ljuboten resident AQ, who, according to reports by non-governmental organisation, was taken into police custody in mid-August. According to the information provided to the delegation's doctors by the relevant medical and administrative staff, AQ had been found on a street and brought to city hospital in Skopje were he was admitted to the trauma ward at 5.00 a.m. on 13 August 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Then the next paragraph refers to the autopsy protocol for this person known as AQ from Ljuboten. It says: "The notes of the relevant autopsy dated 15 August 2001 from the institute of forensic medicine recorded extremely numerous external injuries (excoriations, bruises, haematomas on forearms, arms, thighs and calfs, posterior thorax and lumbar region) of a shape and topography which indicate their cause to be repeated blows with hard objects." Do you see that, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Take a look at the last sentence of that paragraph. This is what it says: "The forensic pathologist concluded that the cause of AQ's death was traumatic shock." Do you see that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question for you is: Did your committee seek autopsy reports from the institute of forensic medicine in Skopje related to persons who were detained at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. If your committee had seen a report such as this, would that have been relevant to the opinion of the report that was produced?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: It is sure that the committee would have initiated other activities, but it is not us who investigate it, especially I'm not specialised to investigate homicides or violent crimes but we would have asked that from the experts in charge of this topic or issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In 2001 how long had you been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: In the entire 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I mean -- let me ask the question this. Tell us again, what year did you join the police force?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So in 2001, you would have been -- you had been a police officer for 26 years?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It didn't occur to you to try to review medical records in Skopje city hospital or autopsy reports in the institute of forensic medicine as part of the work of the committee?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I think I was clear in my previous statement. I was one of the three members of the committee with a exceptionally large number of activities I was in charge with, and I assisted the president of the committee as I could, in respect of the affairs carried out by the uniformed police, and it is up to the criminal police to investigate the incidents like this. I didn't say that nothing has been done. I just said that I was not aware of that. We could assume that the criminal police also processed this case but never came to a specific results in order to inform me that they have found something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could 65 ter 257 be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P380, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, could you please turn to what is tab 5 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P352, Your Honours. It was admitted a week or two ago. If the Macedonian version could be shown to the witness, please. Could the page be turned to -- it's probably now the third page, which is actually the first page of the report. We see the words -- Mr. Usher. And could we please go back a page on the screen, please. That's it. This is the second page in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn to the second page in the Macedonian version. General Galevski, this is a report called crimes against civilians, abuses by Macedonian forces in Ljuboten, August 10 to 12, 2001. Do you see that? Do you see that title?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This report was published by an organisation called Human Rights Watch and it was published in early September 2001. If we could turn to what is page 2 of the report which would be the third page in the Macedonian version, so if we can go forward one page in the English version, please. Looking for an ERN U000-0100. Okay, can we go forward another page, please. General Galevski, do you see the word "summary" at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a summary of this report and if you move down to paragraph 3 it says this: "Macedonian police forces committed serious abuses during their three-day operation in Ljuboten." Further on in that paragraph it says: "During their Sunday house-to-house attack, police forces shot dead six civilians. One man was killed by police as he tried to close the door to his home when the police entered the yard. Two men were summarily executed by police after they were taken out of the basement in which they were hiding. Another three civilians were shot dead by police after they attempted to flee their home, which had been set afire by police shelling. Two paragraphs further down there's a paragraph beginning with: "The abuse continued." Do you see that, General Galevski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "The abuse continued for the hundreds of ethnic Albanian civilians who tried to flee Ljuboten. At least three men were beaten unconscious by ethnic Macedonian vigilantes in view of the Macedonian police and one was shot and wounded as he attempted to flee the beating. The next section says: "Over 100 men were arrested and taken to police stations in Skopje where they were subjected to severe beatings." Then the next sentences: "Atulla Qaili, age 35, was taken away alive from the village by police officers and his badly beaten and mutilated corpse was later recovered by family members from the city morgue." The next paragraph begins: "The Ljuboten operation was carried out by the Macedonian Ministry of Interior's regular and reservist police troops." General Galevski, did your committee know about these allegations before it wrote its report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I read something in the newspapers, if I'm not wrong, if I'm not mistaken. But I have a comment. If I would have read this material at that time I would have surely reacted because as it is mentioned here, there has never been a three-day operation in the village of Ljuboten. Because if one would speak of an operation, that operation lasted for longer period of time because this operations lasted for months, because the tasks of our troops were to guard Skopje, they never acted in Ljuboten because Ljuboten was one of the more peaceful villages at that time because it was known that it is used by the terrorist groups as a logistical base, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, about --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: But there have never been any serious things in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. You say it was known that the village of Ljuboten was used by the terrorist groups as a logistical base. Tell me, would that knowledge have affected the way the committee carried out its investigation?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you said a minute ago that it was known that the village of Ljuboten was used by the terrorist groups as a logistical base. So what I want to know is: Would the knowledge that the village -- that the terrorists were using the village of Ljuboten as a logistical base have affected the way the committee carried out and focussed its investigation?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI
utterances.text: It had no impact at all to the conclusion of the commission. And I will repeat again the biggest impact was by the fact that we were not able to enter the village of Ljuboten and make an on-site investigation. That was the main goal of our task, but if you ask me why, if we knew that there were individuals who were terrorists in that village, I say it more responsibly the Macedonian police never took some rigorous or, as it mentions here, I don't think, like overstepping of forces or similar qualifications in places where there were civilians. On the contrary, only -- even on our expense or even not enforcing our tasks completely, the police tried to maintain the peace and order when it was positioned at the check-points in order to avoid the suffering of civilians, and I do not agree with these statements and qualifications because they are arbitrarious [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, there is a noise coming from our booth. If it bothers you, we should call a technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a bit difficult for me to see the time but it appears to be very close to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is virtually 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Should we break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We resume tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15. So we must interrupt the evidence now, and if you could return tomorrow. Thank you, General. We adjourn now for the evening.
